lead_headline: Restaurant pipeline jumps to 47 active leads as Mendocino Farms opens second Denver location and Otra Vez Cantina resurfaces after pandemic closure

restaurant.blurb: 4 new leads today expand active roster to 47 total (24 openings, 23 closures)—Tuesday bump adds Mendocino Farms' Highlands debut (3453 W 32nd Ave, second Denver outpost from California chain), Otra Vez Cantina's pandemic comeback (CBD location reopened yesterday after multi-year hiatus), plus Aurora's Chaton Bakery website launch near H Mart and The Barn South Broadway closure confirmation in Englewood. Opening leads now edge closures 24-23 after Monday's brief balance—Mendocino expansion mirrors earlier Union Station activity (C Burger, G-Que, Ogo Korean BBQ clustered launches). Week's pattern: downtown/near-downtown hospitality build continues while suburban closures accumulate (CPK Cherry Creek, multiple Dairy Queens, Safeway Aurora all confirmed shuttered). Pipeline tilts net-positive for first time since weekend.

foreclosure.blurb: 30 filings this week hold prior week's floor after five-week descent (49→42→33→30)—decline arrested at 30-filing threshold, suggesting March baseline discovered. 39 auctions scheduled next seven days, $11.2M aggregate exposure unchanged from Sunday count. Arapahoe's $2.24M South Columbine Circle remains week's sole seven-figure property, Weld's $618K Falcon Drive ranks second. County distribution stable: Weld 395 active cases, El Paso 375, Arapahoe 360—exurban concentration persists. Filing trajectory flattened: 9% weekly drop (versus 21-22% prior weeks) indicates deceleration into spring floor range. If 30-filing baseline sustains through March close, seasonal pattern aligns with 2025 comparables—no distressed inventory surge materializing despite earlier February spike concerns.

reputation.blurb: 3 mentions yesterday sustain seven-day total at 39 citations across 11 sources—down 22% from prior week's 50, breaking four-week 43-50 stability range. Denver Post share drops to 33% (13 of 39, versus 36% prior week), Instagram holds 8 pickups, social platforms contribute 9 combined. Notable detections: Traverse Fitness Instagram tease (South Broadway-to-Highlands expansion), Cherry Creek demolition update, upein.edu.pe archive republish. Week's decline driven by Post pickup compression (16→13) rather than source diversification—11 unique outlets unchanged week-over-week. Google News RSS captures 97% discovery (38 of 39). Pattern shift: launch-era 48-53 range descended to 43-45 plateau, now testing 39 floor—suggests either seasonal March dip or recalibration after initial partnership honeymoon. Four-week moving average now 44 daily mentions, down from 47.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +2 yesterday (2 new, 0 canceled) lifts MTD to +25 (+1.6/day), 90-day cumulative to +87. Monday extends weekend's zero-churn streak—three consecutive days without cancellations after mid-week March 12 volatility. Seven-day window now +17 net (22 new, 5 canceled), 2.8x improvement over prior week's +6 (30 new, 24 canceled). Retention compression continues: 0.7/day churn this week versus 3.4/day prior—cancellation discipline drives gains as much as acquisition pace. March's 1.6/day rate now exceeds YTD's 1.3/day benchmark by 23%. Two-week pattern: early-month Mar 3-5 turbulence (−4 low) resolved into stable +1 to +6 range, with March 9 (+6) and March 16 (+4) peaks anchoring momentum. Three-day zero-churn run (Mar 14-16) unprecedented in 14-day window—sustainability test arrives if pattern holds through week's close.
